Hot spots and how long they last

Source: R/hotspot.R
hotspot_persistence.Rd

Counts incidents in square cells of side cell (kilometres for longitude and latitude, map units otherwise) for each period and reports, per period: the incidents, the cells with any, the share of the ever-active cells that holds half the incidents, the hot cells (the top share of the ever-active cells with the most incidents, with the cells tied at the cut included unless the tie would more than double the hot set) and their share of the incidents, and the Jaccard overlap of the hot set with the previous period's (shared hot cells over cells hot in either). Per cell: the incidents in all, and in how many periods it was hot.

Usage

hotspot_persistence(
  lon,
  lat,
  period,
  cell = 0.25,
  top = 0.05,
  coords = c("lonlat", "planar")
)

Arguments

lon, lat

Incident coordinates: longitude and latitude in degrees, or planar coordinates with coords = "planar".

period

The period of each incident (a year, a month, a date); periods are taken in sorted order.

cell

Side of a grid cell: kilometres for longitude and latitude, map units otherwise.

top

Share of the ever-active cells counted as hot in each period.

coords

"lonlat" or "planar".

Value

An object of class rmbl_hotspot: periods (one row per period; tied_in counts the cells made hot only by a tie with the k-th busiest, tied_out the tied cells left out when the tie would have made more than twice k cells hot, which printing says), cells (one row per ever-active cell, with its centre in the input's units), and the settings. Points at (0, 0), the raw exports' "no location", are dropped, and longitudes across the antimeridian are taken on one side of it.

Details

The ever-active cells (a cell with at least one incident in some period) are the base for the shares, so the empty land and water inside a city's bounding box do not dilute the concentration.

Examples

b <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "tps_break_enter_d14_2024.csv",
                          package = "rmoriebricklayer"))
b <- b[!is.na(b$lon), ]
q <- quarters(as.Date(b$occ_date))
h <- hotspot_persistence(b$lon, b$lat, q, cell = 0.3)
h$periods
#>   period incidents active_cells cells_for_half share_for_half hot_cells tied_in
#> 1     Q1       128           77             22      0.1582734        11       4
#> 2     Q2       133           74             22      0.1582734         7       0
#> 3     Q3       112           70             19      0.1366906         7       0
#> 4     Q4       135           72             23      0.1654676         4       0
#>   tied_out hot_share jaccard_previous
#> 1        0 0.3281250               NA
#> 2        0 0.2255639        0.2857143
#> 3        0 0.2678571        0.1666667
#> 4       12 0.1333333        0.1000000
plot(h)
